title: Ableton Production and Headless Orchestration Knowledge Base
purpose: Convert official documentation, long-form tutorials, visual evidence, factory presets, and native-engine audits into grounded production guidance that can be executed or explicitly tracked as unsupported.

method.corpus: Official Ableton articles plus diversified YouTube tutorials, English subtitles, chapters, targeted frames, and OCR.
method.synthesis: Curated production principles are linked to automatically ranked timestamped evidence, device families, roles, recipes, and current native-engine capability records.

evidenceLevels.synthesized: A reusable production conclusion assembled from multiple observed examples.
evidenceLevels.executable: The required device or preset path is currently render-proven headlessly.
evidenceLevels.partial: The device renders, but some routing, automation, preset, or nested-rack semantics remain incomplete.
evidenceLevels.unknown: No tutorial evidence or engine proof currently exists.

method.warning: Tutorial frequency is not an endorsement. Numeric values extracted from speech/OCR are candidates, not verified presets, until an audible fixture passes.

learned.title: Give every sound a job before choosing devices
learned.summary: Richness comes from complementary roles—fundamental, body, transient, air, motion, and space—not from placing a large chain on every channel.
rules: Name the spectral, rhythmic, stereo, and depth role of each layer.
Delete or mute a layer that duplicates another role without adding contrast.
Judge processing in the full arrangement, not only in solo.
failureModes: Every channel is full-range, wide, and reverberant.
More layers increase masking but not perceived detail.

Driving distortion with uncontrolled sub or resonance.

A widened wet branch cancels or smears the mono fundamental.

searchIndex.title: Give every sound a job before choosing devices
searchIndex.text: richness comes from complementary roles—fundamental, body, transient, air, motion, and space—not from placing a large chain on every channel. name the spectral, rhythmic, stereo, and depth role of each layer. delete or mute a layer that duplicates another role without adding contrast. judge processing in the full arrangement, not only in solo. eq8 stereogain spectrumanalyzer arrangement bass drums lead pad mix-bus

searchIndex.title: Serial order is part of the sound
searchIndex.text: filtering before distortion changes what generates harmonics; filtering after distortion changes what remains. the same principle applies to dynamics, modulation, and space. state the purpose of each stage and why it precedes the next one. put corrective filtering before nonlinear stages when unwanted energy should not create harmonics. use post-processing to contain level, bandwidth, and stereo consequences. eq8 autofilter roar saturator compressor2 reverb bass drums lead pad mix-bus

searchIndex.title: Nonlinear devices are input-level dependent
searchIndex.text: amp, saturator, roar, compression, and many analog-modeled devices produce different texture when their input level changes, so gain staging must be declarative. record pre-device gain and post-device trim as part of the patch. level-match bypass comparisons. treat louder as a measurement error, not automatic improvement. stereogain amp saturator roar gluecompressor limiter bass drums lead mix-bus

searchIndex.title: Parallel chains preserve identity while adding character
searchIndex.text: a dry path can retain transient and pitch definition while a wet path supplies distortion, compression, modulation, or ambience. define dry and wet gain independently. band-limit or time-limit the wet branch when it competes with the source. check phase and latency before interpreting the blend. audioeffectgroupdevice audiobranchmixerdevice roar compressor2 reverb bass drums lead pad spatial
